.report — tell the house about someone

.report <name> <what happened> files a one-line report; .report
<name> alone opens the editor for a longer one (.end files it,
.abort discards). It works exactly like .mail, with one difference:
the message does not go to <name>. It goes to the report box, and
<name> is what it is about.

You cannot report yourself. Reports are held encrypted, like mail,
and are read only by whoever this house has given .read_report to —
by default the owner, so that a report about staff does not land
in front of staff.

Your report is signed. Whoever reads it sees your name beside it,
and the name of the person you reported. That is on purpose: a
report nobody can attribute is an accusation with no one behind it,
and it cannot be followed up or weighed.

Nobody ELSE is told — not the room, and not the person you named.
What you wrote is not logged, and neither name is written down
anywhere in the clear; both are held encrypted with the report.

If someone who can read reports is online, they are told at once
that a report has arrived — never what it says. Otherwise they see
it at their next login.
